headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways plausible; compliance risk is also elevated by Replit secrets handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and acts inside a persistent workspace. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from Plane can be copied into Replit Agent inputs and treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads or notes are copied into a Replit workspace for agent processing, THEN injected instructions can reach Replit Agent.
IF the operator uses shared text artifacts as prompts without sanitization, THEN prompt injection is possible.
mitigations: Sanitize copied content before pasting into Replit Agent.
Use a separate staging file for untrusted Plane exports.
Add a manual review step before any agent follows instructions from uploaded content.
Restrict Replit Agent to trusted workspaces only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, and Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Replit Agent also has broad network egress and handles Replit Secrets, so if Plane content is moved into the Repl workspace, sensitive data can be exposed or transmitted. The pair lacks an explicit isolation boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Plane issues, files, or notes contain secrets or regulated data and are copied into the Repl workspace, THEN Replit Agent can read them.
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to external services during normal operation, THEN copied Plane data can leak off-platform.
mitigations: Do not copy sensitive Plane artifacts into Replit workspaces.
Redact secrets before transfer between agents.
Use separate projects for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Review outbound network destinations before running the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Plane is a separate system that can also manage files and task artifacts. If both are pointed at the same mutable repository or synced workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git history. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or synced directory, THEN concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Replit Agent commits while Plane-derived artifacts are being updated, THEN git state can diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Check git status before every commit.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or merge arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can produce issues, tasks, and roadmaps that Replit Agent may use as implementation input, and Replit Agent can then act on that input inside a live Repl. That creates a default pathway where unverified task text becomes code or deployment changes. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, but the blast radius is bounded by the workspace.
conditions: IF Plane output is used as the sole specification for Replit Agent actions, THEN errors can cascade into code or deployment changes.
IF no human verification step exists between Plane tasks and Replit execution, THEN mistaken instructions propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of Plane outputs before execution.
Cross-check task text against source code or deployment state.
Limit Replit Agent to read-only analysis for first pass.
Use checklists for any code or shell action.
requires-engineering: add automated validation before writes.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane touches files, images, notes, and issues, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated data from Plane enters Replit Secrets or the Repl workspace, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty again favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or other regulated data from Plane is placed into a Replit workspace, THEN compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to copied artifacts and Replit keeps workspace history, THEN subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit workspaces.
Use synthetic or masked data for agent runs.
Document data residency before transfer.
Review retention settings for both systems.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
